 Judgment
This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is stated that on 19.12.2023 at about 5.30 a.m., Petitioner was walking to have tea after dropping off passengers and parking his Auto near Ramakrishna Lodge on SC Road, in front of Ramakrishna Lodge, Bangalore City, at that time, the driver of the Auto bearing Reg.

No.KA-03-AG-0869 drove the same at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed Ramakrishna vs Ramalingam K on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48954150/
1 against the petitioner.
Due to the impact, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to KIMS Hospital, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, wherein he was taken treated as an inpatient and has spent a sum of 5,00,000/- towards his medical and other incidental expenses.
3. He was working as a Auto Driver and was earning Rs.35,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and lost his income.

As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent.
4.
In response to the petition notice the respondent did not turn up, thus the order of exparte is passed.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following points arise for my consideration :-
1.Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a Road traffic Accident on 19.2.2023 at about 5.30 a.m., near Ramakrishna Lodge, on S.C.
Road, infront of Ramakrishna Lodge, Bangalore City, due to rash and negligent riding by the driver of Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AG-0869?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, what amount ?
3. What order ?
6. To substantiate the claim, the Petitioner has examined as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P1 to P16.
in support of his case, Dr.Chetan A. Orthopedic Surgeon at Hosmat Hospital is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.17 to P.19 7.
I have heard the arguments of counsel for Petitioner and have perused the material on record.

8. My findings to the above points are as under:
Point No.1: In the Affirmative.
Point No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Point No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. POINT NO.1:-
In order to substantiate the case, the Petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of his examination in chief and examined as PW-1.
He has reiterated the averments of the petition.

10. Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR in connecting to Cr.No.22/2023 registered by the Upparpet Police against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 of IPC and Sec.187, 134(b) of MV Act.
Ex.P2 is the first information statement.
Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar.

Ex.P.4 is the the spot sketch Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is the Ramakrishna vs Ramalingam K on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48954150/
2 Charge sheet in connecting to Cr.No.22/2023 registered by the Upparpet Police against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 338 of IPC and under Sec.134(B), 187, 146,
196, 56 and 192 of IMV Act.

11. On perusal of entire materials available on record it appears that on 19.12.2023 at about 5.30 a.m., Petitioner was walking to have tea after dropping off passengers and parking his Auto near Ramakrishna Lodge on SC Road, in front of Ramakrishna Lodge, Bangalore City, at that time, the driver of the Auto bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AG-0869 drove the same at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
As per wound certificate the petitioner has sustained grievous as well as simple injuries i.e., fracture neck of femur right.
Neither the respondent has appeared before this court nor the contested the case.
There is no evidence to disbelieve or rebut the evidence placed by the petitioner with regard to the alleged accident.
The Charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle and all the records corroborate with the evidence of the Petitioner.
Thereby this tribunal concludes that the accident was caused due to negligence of driver of the offending vehicle and thereby the petitioner sustained grievous injury in a road traffic accident.
Thus, point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
12. POINT NO.2 :-As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained fracture of neck of femur right.
Doctor opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.
13. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to KIMS Hospital, after first aid, he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was doing Auto driver and earning a sum of 35,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

14. The Petitioner has examined Dr. Chetan, Orthopedic Surgeon at Hosmat Hospital, as Pw-2 and he has produced the 3 documents at Ex.P.17 to Ex.P19.
15.

PW-4 has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA and treated at Hosmat Hospital and Petitioner has sustained fracture neck of femur right and he was treated in the Hosmat hospital with
Further he underwent right hip Bipolar Hemi- Arthroplasty on 27.12.2023 and discharged on 31.12.2023.
PW-2 has examined the Petitioner clinically and radiologically while assessing disability.
He has assessed the total disability of the Right lower limb at 43% and whole body physical disability at 14%.
16. It is pertinent to note that PW2 has assessed only physical disability and not the functional disability.
Therefore, considering that the grievous injury and considering the difficulties, avocation and evidence of PW-2 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner
, the functional disability is assessed at 9%.
17. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 62 years and in the wound certificate and other medical record it was mentioned age of the petitioner as 62 years.

Ex.P.10 Aadhar card shows Ramakrishna vs Ramalingam K on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48954150/
3 that he was born of the year 1962.

Thereby it is proper to consider the age petitioner mentioned in the petition and Ex.P.10 Aadhar card for the purpose of ascertaining the compensation and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 7.
18.
The Petitioner states that he was aged about 62 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was doing Auto Driver and was earning Rs.35,000/-P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work.
He is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

19. In this case the petitioner has stated the he was doing Auto Driver and was earning Rs.35,000/-
P.M.
However, the petitioner has not produced any document to substantiate his income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the national income chart of the Lok Adalath.
20. On perusal of the record, it appears that the age of the petitioner as on date of the alleged accident was about 61 years.
The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 16,000/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
21. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Looking into the nature of injuries, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.

As the Petitioner is doing driving work,
considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 9%.

Thus, loss of future income comes to Rs.16,000 x 12 x 7 x 9/100= Rs.1,20,960/-
towards loss of future income.
22. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has suffered and was inpatient for a period of 13 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain.
Hence, I am of the opinion that an amount of .25,000/- would be just and proper compensation towards pain and sufferings.
23. Loss of amenities of life: due to injuries the petitioner is unable to do his day today activities and face hardships.
Thereby the Petitioner is awarded .20,000/- towards loss of amenities of life.
24. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on medical bills at Ex.P.14.
On perusal of these medical bills, it reveals that the Petitioner has spent .3,50,898/- towards medical expenses.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of .3,50,898/-
towards Medical Expenses.
25. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P.8-Discharge summary shows that the Petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Hosmat hospital, Bangalore, from 19.12.2023 to 31.12.2023 i.e. for a period of 13 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .15,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.

sentences.text: Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 13 days admitted in the hospital as inpatient and around one and half months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 2 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, Petitioner is awarded .32,000/-
towards loss of earning during laid up period.

27. Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount No.
1. Loss of future earnings . 1,20,960/ -
2. Pain and Sufferings . 25,000/-
3. Loss of amenities . 20,000/-
4.

Medical expenses . 3,50,898/-
5. Conveyance, Food, . 15,000/-
Nourishment & Attendant charges 6. Loss of income during . 32,000/-
 laid up period
Liability:

As it is already held that the accident was due to the negligence of driver of offending vehicle, Respondent No.1 being the owner is liable to pay the above compensation to the Petitioner with interest @ 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer point No.2 partly in the affirmative.

29. POINT NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to point Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,63,858/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.

Respondent is liable to pay the aforesaid amount within three months from the date Ramakrishna vs Ramalingam K on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48954150/
5 of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 2 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to him through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

(SHYLA S.M.) II Addl. Judge & ACJM Member, MACT Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru ANNEXURE
